- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for sustained positive sentiment.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >75% increase from prior 30d) — add 3–8% buffer to forecast for momentum carryover.
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (days 1–7) — apply 10–15% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Mean-reversion bias in low sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day if sentiment remains below 0.2 for >3 days.
- Lagged overreaction in 30d forecasts — if true outcome deviates >5% from 30d forecast, check if sentiment was high 3–5 days prior — if yes, reduce forecast by 2–5%.
- Avoid overconfidence in high sentiment + high recent price volatility — cap forecast increase at +3% per day if sentiment > 0.7 and volatility > 1.5%.
- If sentiment drops sharply after forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days to reflect sentiment decay.
